text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Public Authority for Industry studies privatisation.
- Health Ministry to announce new organisational structure next month, official says.

- Head of Municipal Council expects wide debate at council's next meeting after he nominated a woman engineer to the post of assistant secretary. Kuwaiti women hold senior posts in the conservative Gulf Arab state but they are not allowed to vote or stand elections for parliament and the Municipal Council.
- MP says imposing higher fees on public services will not end budget deficit. Civil servants wages must not be reduced.
- Kuwaiti pilot sues national flag carrier Kuwait Airways Corp for allegedly unfairly firing him.
- Bank of Kuwait and the Middle East to upgrade services in 1997.

- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah to receive a message from Syrian President Hafez al-Assad. Syrian Vice-President Abdel- Halim Khaddam and Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara are due in Kuwait on Monday.
- Average direct annual wage, including salaries and allowances, for expatriates rose to 1,482 dinars ($4,960) from 1,396 dinars ($4,670) in 1989, study says.
